prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the 2000 portrait of Jackie Leven with a raised glass. Make this SAME portrait a little more abstract and clearly drawn, matching the graphic economy of the approved series.
Image 2 is the STYLE reference only: the approved Doll-by-Doll-era illustration. Use its broad facial planes and bold broken strokes, not its younger face, hairstyle or anatomy.
Image 3 is the ORIGINAL photograph, used only to keep Jackie's true likeness and the natural glass-holding gesture anchored.

Preserve the edit target's exact facial proportions, age, expression, eye and nose placement, head angle, raised-glass pose, composition, hand anatomy, clothing and canvas. The glass is mandatory and must remain fully visible. Do not move or remove it.

The change must be structural simplification, NOT just adding a texture filter:
FACE: replace the many small dabs and continuous photographic modelling with a small number of broad calm neutral-grey ink planes, around three or four main values. Forehead, cheek and neck have open areas and selective directional brush marks rather than detailed skin. Describe eyes, brows, nose and lips with a few precise strong marks. Keep their shapes and natural anatomy faithful. No new wrinkles, caricature, geometric facet pattern or smooth airbrush shading.
HAIR: substantially reduce the fine curling filaments and shiny individual strands. Group the curls into broad dark masses interrupted by a few energetic sweeping dry-brush gestures. Retain the same overall curly silhouette and hairline.
HAND: retain its correct relaxed grip and five-digit anatomy, but reduce the small skin shading, knuckles and nails to broad light/shadow marks. No photographic hand detail.
GLASS: simplify the cut-crystal decoration strongly. Keep the elliptical rim, the two side contours, the thick base and a suggestion of the liquid, using broken grey strokes and dark negative space. Only a few short diagonal cut-glass gestures remain; eliminate the intricate engraved/reflected pattern and sparkling facets. It must still read clearly as a transparent tumbler held up in a toast. No colour in the liquid.
CLOTHES: a few confident dark collar and shoulder gestures; let the jacket and chest dissolve into mostly untouched darkness.
Mark-making should be visibly hand-made, with irregular dry-brush ends and lively gaps, more like ink drawn with a worn brush than an oil painting. No repeated pebble-like microtexture, digital posterization, vector cutouts or glossy impasto. Achieve the abstraction seen in image 2 while retaining image 1's likeness and gesture.

Maintain the same dark neutral palette, slightly subdued if needed: near-black anthracite #0d0f12 background, charcoal and muted neutral-grey marks only. No sepia, brown, beige, cream, colour tint or white glare. Do not brighten the face, hair or glass. Keep natural positive light/shadow, dark eyes and nostrils within lighter grey planes. Preserve soft broken outer edges merging into the webpage background.
Same vertical 4:5, no text, no logo, no signature, no border or background objects. One standalone portrait, recognizably the same image but with fewer, stronger drawn shapes and much less fine detail.
